title: Token delta encoding and adaptive-stack patterns for metric timelines & rollout lanes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: define a compact, interoperable token schema ("delta encoding") for visual and interaction variants, and design an adaptive stacking pattern for metric tiles and rollout lanes that preserves density while keeping critical cost signals visible. Scope: token naming conventions, variable override strategy for rollouts, responsive stacking rules for 3- to 1-column breakpoints, motion guidelines for state transitions, and accessibility contrast targets. Deliverables: Figma component library update, token mapping guide, platform integration PR, design QA checklist.
updates: 2025-02-20: Ticket created after cross-functional scoping workshop with PM and runtime team. Identified mismatches in current token overrides causing visual drift during canary rollouts.
2025-02-22: Low-fidelity prototypes for adaptive stacking reviewed with engineering; agreed on canonical breakpoints and collapse-to-compact mode at <= 600px.
2025-02-26: Mid-fidelity Figma components implemented; token delta approach documented: base token + small delta layers for rollout states (canary, degraded, fallback).
2025-02-28: Accessibility pass: increased label contrast for cost sparkline and ensured 4.5:1 for small text in compact mode. Noted edge case where color-only legend used — added icon affordances.
2025-03-01: Design review scheduled. Feedback from PM: request to add telemetry hooks (toggle state) for A/B rollout. Follow-up: add binding spec for telemetry IDs.
Next steps: finalize Figma components, handoff tokens to platform engineers, create integration PR, schedule design QA during runtime-1.20 sprint.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive density harms scanability; chose progressive disclosure for secondary metrics. Kernel: prefer token overrides over duplicated components to minimize Figma library bloat. Engineering asked for explicit token-to-css mapping; to be provided in PR.
